key_insight: A magnetic field can trigger Leidenfrost-like rebound in ferrofluid droplets at substrate temperatures below the usual zero-field Leidenfrost threshold, creating a new magneto-Leidenfrost effect (MLFE).
engineering_relevance: This enables field-controlled, near-frictionless droplet transport and targeted activation for thermal management and droplet-handling systems.
method: High-speed imaging of impacting aqueous Fe2O3 ferrofluid droplets on heated substrates under varying magnetic fields
Parametric study using Weber number, magnetic Bond number, and maximum spread factor to separate inertia, magnetic, and viscocapillary effects
Theoretical framework to explain magnetic spreading enhancement, rebound onset, and post-impact regimes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally observed shifts in rebound onset, residence time, and fragmentation behavior across substrate temperature, magnetic field strength, and nanoparticle concentration, with theory matching the measurements.
watch_item: MLFE performance appears sensitive to substrate temperature, magnetic field strength, and particle loading, so results may be difficult to generalize across fluids or surface conditions without careful calibration.
paper_title: The magneto-Leidenfrost effect in ferrofluid droplets
